reason: The cited evidence discusses general concepts (grain boundaries and sinks for defect annihilation, HEA stability) but provides no specific data on Hf addition to WMoTaNbV, Hf-rich precipitate formation, or their thermal/mechanical effects. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Hf addition to WMoTaNbV forms fine Hf-rich carbide/oxide precipitates
These precipitates are thermally stable at ~900 °C
Precipitates pin dislocations, enhancing yield strength
Precipitates act as defect sinks, promoting point-defect recombination
This reduces irradiation-induced defect clustering, swelling, and embrittlement
